subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this generated-versus-external MCPorter routing contract for existing QMD users, where bare stdio definitions move to per-agent generated config and daemon identities while customized definitions remain owned by their original config file?
rationale: The patch can be technically correct while still changing upgrade behavior, daemon ownership, and memory-index routing for existing installations; repository policy requires a human owner to accept that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Approve the routing contract
options.body: Accept the per-agent generated path for bare stdio QMD servers, preserve customized definitions externally, and merge after exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Land a narrower repair
options.body: Split out process-environment isolation first and defer generated-config classification until its upgrade semantics are separately approved.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep current behavior until maintainers define a different canonical MCPorter ownership and migration model.

recommendation.title: Approve the routing contract
recommendation.body: Accept the per-agent generated path for bare stdio QMD servers, preserve customized definitions externally, and merge after exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent QMD memory work and the latest release history make this the strongest available owner for the compatibility decision.
